rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, three pre-real amendments from synthetic validation (196 runs on three real schedules, with and without contemporaneous convergence), 34 replication folders and 3 native tests (NE42, NE41, #51) with dated predictions and verdicts, rivals (phase, shared sources) and both embedding models, a labelled post hoc amendment after the real data, and a confirm script dry-run on stand-ins (not run). Missing: holdout run, a lag-resolved chance model, and validation of the post hoc estimator beyond stylised worlds.
rationale.faithfulness: The core prediction is refuted: no rise of echo with backlog in any period (raw upper bound +0.0016 per doubling, about 5% of the synthetic effect), a message-level copy share of about 0 at every backlog, and no response to NE42's backlog jump or NE41's erasures. The pre-registered estimator itself proved invalid on real data (contemporaneous convergence), so the refutation rests on the post hoc bound and lag profiles. Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D0 E0 F1 G1 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A diagnostic any operator can compute: compare near-duplicates between read messages and unread messages at the same lag before calling anything copying. In the village, simultaneous convergence accounts for the semantic near-duplication, and load does not make agents parrot. It corrects shared instruments (2-h echo flags) and readings in H12 and H07, but gives no lever.

one_line: Backlog does not make agents echo (raw upper bound +0.0016 per doubling, ~5% of the H57 effect); most near-duplication is simultaneous convergence, not copying.

v2.claim: A large read backlog does not make agents copy what they read: the raw read-set echo, an upper bound, rises by at most +0.0016 per doubling of backlog (gte +0.0012; <= 5% of the synthetic H57 effect) across 34 non-holdout periods and the NE42, NE41 and #51 natives; below 15 s mutually unread pairs are near-copies as often as read pairs, so most near-duplication is contemporaneous convergence.

ladder.factor: base: secondary (P1 pre-registered; the verdict rests on Amendment 2 estimators built after the first real-data run)
identified: raw echo and the lag-matched count recover the planted slope on real schedules, unbiased in convergence worlds (also the null calibration; one design)
robust to instruments and estimators (both encoders; raw, lag-matched, filtered, day FE all show no rise)
intervention partly consistent (NE42 backlog +0.59 log2 with no dose response; NE41 erasures null; goal-confounded)
penalty: verdict and the convergence account are post hoc

v2.adjudication_note: V judgement: the coordinator valued only the backlog negative (V 1.5); the blind rater valued the convergence finding as a large, general, ready rule for echo monitors (V 4) and called it M1. Ruling: the claim keeps both parts, the convergence part carries the decision value, but its signature was diagnosed post hoc and the replacement chance model is not built, so V is material without generality or readiness credit and the mechanism level is M0. Credence credits the synthetic once and the two-encoder robustness, with a post hoc penalty.
